title: The Agentic Information Economy
gist: Shuwei Fang argues that as AI agents act on information rather than merely consume it, errors become consequential actions, requiring an information ecology that can question inputs and propagate corrections. Teaser-length excerpt.

themes.theme: Information as action under AI agents

insights.claim: Information is undergoing a category change: it is becoming something machines act on, so errors stop being mere digital impressions and become actions with far-reaching consequences.
insights.speaker: SHUWEI FANG
insights.so_what: Agent-driven workflows raise the cost of bad data, favoring data-verification and correction infrastructure.
insights.quote: Information is undergoing a category change.

insights.claim: An internet run by AI agents needs not just reliable data but an information ecology able to question its own inputs and transmit corrections when information changes.
insights.speaker: SHUWEI FANG
insights.so_what: Points to demand for provenance, auditing and correction-propagation tooling.

insights.claim: Better data or putting a human back in the loop will not suffice as safeguards for an agentic information system; the system needs safeguards of its own.
insights.speaker: SHUWEI FANG
insights.so_what: Challenges the standard human-oversight answer to agent risk.
insights.quote: Better data or putting a human back in the loop will not suffice.

insights.claim: Whether the agentic information economy will serve private interests or the public good remains undetermined.
insights.speaker: SHUWEI FANG
insights.so_what: Governance outcome is open; regulatory and market-structure risk.
